tagline: Hairpin turns climb from Bakersville toward Roan Mountain’s forests and grassy balds.
intro: On Highlands of the Roan, the mountain climb follows NC 261 out of Bakersville into Pisgah National Forest. The road winds past creeks and through hairpin turns to Carvers Gap at 5,500 feet. NCDOT includes Highlands of the Roan in its scenic-byway guide, whose stated purpose is to offer routes through North Carolina’s history, geography and culture. At Roan Mountain, spruce-fir forest, rhododendron gardens and grassy balds share the crest.

An earlier road across Carvers Gap supplied John T. Wilder’s mountaintop Cloudland Hotel, completed in 1885. Wilder built the road to carry construction materials uphill and later provision the hotel. Bakersville developed on the route over Roan Mountain into Tennessee. The road from Bakersville to Carvers Gap was once unnumbered, surfaced with gravel and dirt. Between 1949 and 1953, the state took it over and laid asphalt. NC 261 has followed the same routing since its designation.

Begin with Micaville, named for the mica mined there, and Kona on NC 80 near the meeting of the North and South Toe rivers. Bakersville lies in the Cane Creek valley. From town, NC 261 crosses Pumpkin Patch Gap, follows Little Rock Creek through Cookstown and Glen Ayre, then climbs to Carvers Gap. There, the Appalachian Trail crosses the road on the Tennessee line.

moments.title: Kona
moments.text: Kona takes its name from feldspar’s chemistry: K for potassium, O for oxygen and Na for sodium. The community lies on NC 80 near the meeting of the North and South Toe rivers. Founded in 1916, it became the starting point of the Black Mountain Railway and its connection with the South and Western Railroad. Passenger and mixed trains ran daily round trips through Burnsville to Murchison. The Black Mountain line later belonged to the Yancey Railroad. By the 1950s, only freight remained on both lines; the Yancey Railroad ceased operating in 1982. Kona’s post office opened in 1916 and closed in 1953.

moments.title: Bakersville
moments.text: Bakersville’s county-seat role followed the Civil War, when Mitchell County moved its seat here and a courthouse helped spur growth. Commercial demand for mica brought a temporary boom in the 1870s. The old courthouse now in town came later, built in 1907–1908 with cast-stone walls, turret-like corner bays and a square cupola capped by a dome. A new courthouse replaced it in 2003; the older building houses the Board of Elections, Historical Society and Rural Education Partnership. Bakersville also hosts the North Carolina Rhododendron Festival, linking the town with the mountain’s flowers.
moments.notice: The old courthouse has turret-like corner bays and a square cupola topped by a dome.

moments.title: Roan Mountain
moments.text: Carvers Gap divides two different mountain landscapes. To the west, conifers cover Roan High Knob and Roan High Bluff, with rhododendron gardens in Tollhouse Gap between them. East of the gap, Grassy Ridge carries highland meadows with thick grass and few trees across Round Bald, Jane Bald and Grassy Ridge Bald. From the gap’s parking area, the Appalachian Trail crosses the road and climbs Round Bald. A separate paved road connects Carvers Gap to Tollhouse Gap and the Cloudland Trailhead, whose trail crosses the rhododendron gardens. The Appalachian Trail traverses most of Roan’s crest.

practical: Roan Mountain: The paved road from Carvers Gap to Tollhouse Gap is closed in winter. (checked 2026-10-11)
